claim: The Min system determines the bacterial cell division plane using changes in the localization of proteins (a Min wave) that emerges by reaction-diffusion coupling.
source: The Min system, a system that determines the bacterial cell division plane, uses changes in the localization of proteins (a Min wave) that emerges by reaction-diffusion coupling.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations to previous work on the Min system.

claim: Confinement changes the conditions for the emergence of Min waves in microsized spaces.
source: Here, by using a microsized fully confined space to mimic live cells, we revealed that confinement changes the conditions for the emergence of Min waves.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through experiments comparing 2D planar membranes to confined microdroplets.

claim: In microsized space, an increased surface-to-volume ratio changed the localization efficiency of proteins on membranes.
source: In the microsized space, an increased surface-to-volume ratio changed the localization efficiency of proteins on membranes, and therefore, suppression of the localization change was necessary for the stable generation of Min waves.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing size-dependent MinE localization (Figure 4).

claim: Suppression of localization change was necessary for the stable generation of Min waves in microsized space.
source: In the microsized space, an increased surface-to-volume ratio changed the localization efficiency of proteins on membranes, and therefore, suppression of the localization change was necessary for the stable generation of Min waves.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments showing that BSA, which suppresses MinE membrane localization, enables Min wave generation (Figure 1D, Figure 3).

claim: Cell-sized space strictly limits parameters for wave emergence because confinement inhibits both the instability and excitability of the system.
source: Furthermore, we showed that the cell-sized space strictly limits parameters for wave emergence because confinement inhibits both the instability and excitability of the system.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by theoretical analysis and simulations (Figures 6-8).

claim: The Min system comprises three proteins called MinC, MinD, and MinE.
source: This system comprises three proteins called MinC, MinD, and MinE, with the localization of MinD and MinE oscillating between one pole and the other as the result of a coupling between biochemical reactions and molecular diffusions (Loose et al., 2008; Rowlett and Margolin, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Min system, supported by citations.

claim: The localization of MinD and MinE oscillates between one pole and the other as the result of coupling between biochemical reactions and molecular diffusions.
source: This system comprises three proteins called MinC, MinD, and MinE, with the localization of MinD and MinE oscillating between one pole and the other as the result of a coupling between biochemical reactions and molecular diffusions (Loose et al., 2008; Rowlett and Margolin, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous work.

claim: MinC inhibits the polymerization of FtsZ by following the Min wave.
source: MinC has no role in the Min wave but rather inhibits the polymerization of a cell division initiation factor (FtsZ) by following the Min wave.
evidence: This is established knowledge about MinC function, supported by citations.

claim: The Min system enforces the initiation of cell division only at the center of cells.
source: This process enforces the initiation of cell division only at the center of cells (Rothfield et al., 2005; Rowlett and Margolin, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Min system function, supported by citations.

claim: Min wave is the only biological RD system reconstituted in vitro.
source: To date, Min wave is the only biological RD system reconstituted in vitro.
evidence: This is a statement of the state of the field at the time of writing.

claim: The reconstitution of Min wave was first shown by spotting a mixture of MinD, MinE, and ATP on two-dimensional planar membranes comprising E. coli polar lipid extract in open geometry.
source: The reconstitution of Min wave was first shown by spotting a mixture of MinD, MinE, and ATP on two-dimensinal (2D) planar membranes comprising E. coli polar lipid extract in open geometry (Loose et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a historical fact about the first in vitro reconstitution, supported by citation.

claim: External environments such as boundary shapes, protein concentrations, and lipid species alter the patterns, velocities, wavelengths and shapes of Min waves.
source: In vitro studies have demonstrated that external environments such as boundary shapes, protein concentrations, and lipid species alter the patterns, velocities, wavelengths and shapes of Min waves (Martos et al., 2013; Zieske and Schwille, 2013; Vecchiarelli et al., 2014; Zieske et al., 2016; Caspi and Dekker, 2016; Denk et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous in vitro studies, supported by multiple citations.

claim: A rod-shape is important in terms of inducing the pole-to-pole oscillation found in living cells.
source: In particular, boundary shapes prepared by structured poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) chambers significantly change the behavior of Min waves, with studies showing that a rod-shape is important in terms of inducing the pole-to-pole oscillation found in living cells (Zieske and Schwille, 2013; Zieske et al., 2016; Caspi and Dekker, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: The effect of confinement in cell-sized spaces on Min wave emergence has been poorly addressed.
source: The critical conditions for Min wave emergence, including environmental effects, have been surveyed in open spaces, but the effect of confinement in cell-sized spaces, which is one of the most remarkable features of living cells, has been poorly addressed.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in the literature that this study addresses.

claim: Some studies have reported reconstitution of Min waves in fully confined cell-sized spaces, but lipid conditions were modified or the spaces were closed after observing wave generation.
source: Although some studies have reported reconstitution of Min waves in fully confined cell-sized spaces (Zieske et al., 2016; Caspi and Dekker, 2016; Litschel et al., 2018), lipid conditions were modified or the spaces were closed after observing wave generation.
evidence: This is a statement about previous work, supported by citations.

claim: The necessity of special treatments suggests that the cell-sized space affects the conditions that are needed for Min wave emergence.
source: The necessity of these treatments suggests that the cell-sized space affects the conditions that are needed for Min wave emergence.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that previous studies required special conditions.

claim: Confinement inside cell-sized space alters both the behaviors of biochemical reactions and molecular diffusion.
source: Recent studies have unveiled that confinement inside cell-sized space alters both the behaviors of biochemical reactions and molecular diffusion (Yanagisawa et al., 2014b; Küchler et al., 2016; Watanabe and Yanagisawa, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from recent studies, supported by citations.

claim: RD waves appear only in limited parameter ranges.
source: Because RD waves appear only in limited parameter ranges (Zhabotinsky et al., 1995; Epstein and Showalter, 1996), encapsulation inside a cell-sized space should shift the conditions that are suitable for Min wave emergence, such as the diffusion and interaction of the wave's elements.
evidence: This is established knowledge about reaction-diffusion systems, supported by citations.

claim: Encapsulation inside a cell-sized space should shift the conditions that are suitable for Min wave emergence.
source: Because RD waves appear only in limited parameter ranges (Zhabotinsky et al., 1995; Epstein and Showalter, 1996), encapsulation inside a cell-sized space should shift the conditions that are suitable for Min wave emergence, such as the diffusion and interaction of the wave's elements.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on established knowledge about RD systems and confinement effects.

claim: Only MinD, MinE, and ATP are necessary and sufficient for the generation of Min waves on 2D planar membranes of E. coli polar lipid extract.
source: Previous studies have reported that only MinD, MinE, and ATP are necessary and sufficient for the generation of Min waves on 2D planar membranes of E. coli polar lipid extract (Loose et al., 2008) (Figure 1A) and in a cell-sized space that is fully confined by using a modified lipid mixture (Zieske et al., 2016; Litschel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: The Min wave in open geometry has been reproduced using materials prepared in the authors' laboratory (sfGFP-MinD and MinE-mCherry).
source: The Min wave in open geometry has been well characterized in many laboratories (Loose et al., 2011; Vecchiarelli et al., 2014; Caspi and Dekker, 2016), and has also been reproduced by using materials prepared in our laboratory (sfGFP-MinD and MinE-mCherry) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: sfGFP-MinD, MinE-mCherry, and ATP are insufficient for Min wave emergence in microdroplets covered with E. coli polar lipids.
source: However, we found that sfGFP-MinD, MinE-mCherry, and ATP are insufficient for Min wave emergence in the microdroplets covered with E. coli polar lipids (Figure 1C, Video 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding demonstrated in Figure 1C and Video 1.

claim: Fluorescent proteins fused with MinD or MinE could not explain the lack of wave occurrence in microdroplets.
source: Use of non-fluorescent tagged MinDE tracked by sfGFP-MinC indicated that fluorescent proteins fused with MinD or MinE could not explain the lack of wave occurrence (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by control experiments using sfGFP-MinC to track non-tagged MinDE.

claim: sfGFP-MinD, MinE-mCherry, and ATP induced Min waves in microdroplets covered with a lipid mixture (85% DOPC and 15% cardiolipin).
source: By contrast, sfGFP-MinD, MinE-mCherry, and ATP induced Min waves in microdroplets covered with a lipid mixture (85% DOPC and 15% cardiolipin), as reported previously (Zieske et al., 2016) (Video 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Video 2, consistent with previous reports.

claim: After encapsulation in a micro-sized space fully covered with lipid, some critical parameters for Min wave emergence differ from those that allow for wave emergence on 2D membranes.
source: These results indicated that after encapsulation in a micro-sized space fully covered with lipid alters, some critical parameters for Min wave emergence differ from those that allow for wave emergence on 2D membranes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations comparing 2D and 3D systems.

claim: Co-supplementation of BSA at high concentration (100 mg/mL) with Min proteins induced Min wave emergence in microdroplets.
source: Remarkably, co-supplementation of BSA at high concentration (100 mg/mL) with Min proteins induced Min wave emergence (Figure 1D, Video 3), whiereas neither PEG8000 nor Ficoll70 induced Min waves (Videos 4 and 5).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding demonstrated in Figure 1D and Video 3.

claim: Neither PEG8000 nor Ficoll70 induced Min waves in microdroplets.
source: Remarkably, co-supplementation of BSA at high concentration (100 mg/mL) with Min proteins induced Min wave emergence (Figure 1D, Video 3), whiereas neither PEG8000 nor Ficoll70 induced Min waves (Videos 4 and 5).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Videos 4 and 5.

claim: Both MinD and MinE should be present at a concentration of around 1 μM to lead the emergence of Min waves in microdroplets with BSA.
source: Varying concentrations of MinD and MinE indicated that both proteins should be present at a concentration of around 1 μM to lead the emergence of Min waves (Figure 1E), consistent with their concentrations in vivo (Shih et al., 2002).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 1E and is consistent with in vivo concentrations.

claim: The Min wave depends on ATP.
source: ATP replacement with ADP or ATPγS, or replacement of MinD with an ATPase-deficient mutant (Zhou et al., 2005), showed that the Min wave depends on ATP (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), as is the case for waves on 2D planar membranes (Loose et al., 2008).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The frequent patterns observed in microdroplets were pole-to-pole oscillations and traveling waves.
source: The frequent patterns observed were pole-to-pole oscillations and traveling waves (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), as noted by a previous study using modified lipids (Zieske et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: MinE was enriched at the tail of the traveling wave.
source: MinE was enriched at the tail of the traveling wave (Figure 1F top) and was enriched at both tails of the wave in pole-to-pole oscillations (Figure 1F bottom).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 1F.

claim: MinE enrichments in microdroplets were similar to those reported previously for traveling waves on 2D planar membranes and for the E ring observed in living cells with pole-to-pole oscillations.
source: These MinE enrichments were similar to those reported previously for traveling waves on 2D planar membranes (Loose et al., 2008), and for the so-called E ring observed in living cells with pole-to-pole oscillations (Rothfield et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous observations, supported by citations.

claim: The diffusion rate of GFP in cytosolic parts at 50 mg/mL BSA was similar to that in non-crowding conditions but decreased at over 100 mg/mL.
source: FCS revealed that the diffusion rate of GFP in cytosolic parts at 50 mg/mL BSA was similar to that in non-crowding conditions but decreased at over 100 mg/mL (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by FCS measurements shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Min waves were generated stably even with 50 mg/mL of BSA.
source: However, we found that Min waves were generated stably even with 50 mg/mL of BSA (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The diffusion rates of MinD on lipid membranes of various sizes of microdroplets decreased only slightly even in 100 mg/mL of BSA.
source: The diffusion rates of MinD on lipid membranes of various sizes of microdroplets decreased only slightly even in 100 mg/mL of BSA (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by FRAP measurements shown in Figure 2B.

claim: BSA does not bind directly to MinD or MinE.
source: The pull-down assay showed that BSA flowed through the Ni-NTA with Min proteins, and therefore, no BSA band was found after eluting MinD or MinE by imidazole. These results indicate that BSA does not bind directly to MinD or MinE.
evidence: This is demonstrated by pull-down assay results shown in Figure 2C.

claim: BSA does not enhance the interactions of the MinDE complex.
source: The pull-down assay using MinDD40AΔ10, which still bound with MinE due to its lack of ATPase activity (Park et al., 2017), also indicates that BSA does not enhance the interactions of the MinDE complex (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by pull-down assay results shown in Figure 2C.

claim: BSA leads MinE to localize differently in cytosolic parts and on membranes.
source: Even though the three above-mentioned effects are not relevant, we found that BSA leads MinE to localize differently in cytosolic parts and on membranes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental observations in Figure 2D.

claim: In the absence of BSA, almost all of the MinD and MinE were localized similarly on membranes.
source: In the absence of BSA, almost all of the MinD and MinE were localized similarly on membranes.
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In the presence of BSA, changes in MinD localization were relatively few, but the localization of MinE on membranes completely disappeared.
source: By contrast, the addition of BSA drastically changed the localization. In the presence of BSA, changes in MinD localization were relatively few, but the localization of MinE on membranes completely disappeared (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The spontaneous localization of MinE cannot be explained by membrane defects.
source: Because sfGFP alone or BSA at low concentration (0.67 mg/mL) does not localize on membranes (Figure 2D), the spontaneous localization of MinE cannot be explained by membrane defects.
evidence: This is demonstrated by control experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The localization of MinE was not driven by protein denaturation.
source: Furthermore, FRAP also showed that MinE-mCherry diffuses faster than sfGFP-MinD in the absence of BSA, which indicates that the localization of MinE was not driven by protein denaturation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by FRAP measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Changes in the localization of MinE are a key factor in the emergence of waves in microdroplets.
source: These results suggest that changes in the localization of MinE are a key factor in the emergence of waves in microdroplets.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations about MinE localization.

claim: The c/m of MinE increased in proportion to BSA concentration.
source: As shown in Figure 3B, the c/m of MinE increased in proportion to BSA concentration.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 3B.

claim: The relation between c/m and the probability of Min wave emergence is sigmoidal as a threshold function.
source: Plots of wave emergence percentage as a function of c/m controlled by BSA concentration showed that its relation is a sigmoidal as a threshold function (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 3C.

claim: Min waves were observed in a small fraction of microdroplets at c/m <0.4 (<1 mg/mL BSA).
source: Min waves were observed in a small fraction of microdroplets at c/m <0.4 (<1 mg/mL BSA), and in almost all microdroplets at c/m >0.7 (>30 mg/mL BSA).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the data in Figure 3C.

claim: Min waves were observed in almost all microdroplets at c/m >0.7 (>30 mg/mL BSA).
source: Min waves were observed in a small fraction of microdroplets at c/m <0.4 (<1 mg/mL BSA), and in almost all microdroplets at c/m >0.7 (>30 mg/mL BSA).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the data in Figure 3C.

claim: E. coli cell extract modulated the c/m of MinE in a similar manner as BSA, although its effect was stronger than BSA.
source: The cell extract modulated the c/m of MinE in a similar manner as BSA, although its effect was stronger than BSA (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 3D.

claim: E. coli cell extract led to the emergence of Min waves in the microdroplets covered with E. coli polar lipid extract.
source: Moreover, the cell extract also led to the emergence of Min waves in the microdroplets covered with E. coli polar lipid extract (Video 7).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Video 7.

claim: The relation between c/m and the probability of Min wave emergence with cell extract was similar to that of BSA concentration.
source: The relation between c/m and the probability of Min wave emergence was similar to that of BSA concentration (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 3E.

claim: High c/m is required for the stable emergence of Min waves in a 3D closed geometry.
source: These results indicated that high c/m is required for the stable emergence of Min waves in a 3D closed geometry.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations about c/m and wave emergence.

claim: Under conditions using macromolecular crowding reagents that do not lead to the emergence of Min waves (PEG8000 and Ficoll70), c/m was as low as and similar to that without BSA.
source: Under conditions using macromolecular crowding reagents that do not lead to the emergence of Min waves (PEG8000 and Ficoll70), c/m was as low as and similar to that without BSA (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 3F.

claim: When the lipid was modified (15% cardiolipin and 85% DOPC), c/m was near 0.4.
source: Then, we checked c/m in the case of microdroplets covered with the modified lipid (15% cardiolipin and 85% DOPC), which causes Min waves without BSA. When the lipid was modified, c/m was near 0.4 (Figure 3F), which is as high as the minimal BSA-associated c/m value required for Min wave emergence.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 3F.

claim: The suppression of attachment of MinE on membrane without the aid of MinD is key to the emergence of Min waves in micro-sized space.
source: These results supported the notion that the suppression of attachment of MinE on membrane without the aid of MinD is key to the emergence of Min waves in micro-sized space.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations about MinE localization and wave emergence.

claim: In smaller microdroplets (<20 μm diameter), c/m was less than 0.2.
source: In smaller microdroplets (<20 μm diameter), c/m was less than 0.2.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the data in Figure 4.

claim: In larger microdroplets (>20 μm diameter), c/m increased in proportion to the amount of MinE.
source: In larger microdroplets (>20 μm diameter), c/m increased in proportion to the amount of MinE.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the data in Figure 4.

claim: The increase in c/m was highly dependent on the concentration of MinE.
source: Moreover, the increase in c/m was highly dependent on the concentration of MinE.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the data in Figure 4.

claim: The diameters of microdroplets in which c/m reached 0.5 were approximately 45 μm at 10 μM MinE, and around 70 μm at 3 μM MinE.
source: The diameters of microdroplets in which c/m reached 0.5 were approximately 45 μm at 10 μM MinE, and around 70 μm at 3 μM MinE (Figure 4).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the data in Figure 4.

claim: In the case of 1 μM MinE, c/m stayed low when the droplet size was less than 130 μm.
source: In the case of 1 μM MinE, c/m stayed low when the droplet size was less than 130 μm (Figure 4).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the data in Figure 4.

claim: In the presence of 10 mg/mL BSA, c/m did not depend on microdroplet size.
source: We also tested the size dependence of c/m in the presence of 10 mg/mL BSA, which is the minimum BSA concentration for Min wave emergence in microdroplets. In this case, c/m did not depend on microdroplet size.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the presence of 10 mg/mL BSA, the value of c/m was higher than 0.7.
source: However, the value of c/m was higher than 0.7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The degree of spontaneous MinE binding shifts the conditions for Min wave emergence.
source: Consistent with our experimental results, the numerical simulations indicated that the degree of spontaneous MinE binding shifts the conditions for Min wave emergence (Figure 5).
evidence: This is demonstrated by computational simulations shown in Figure 5.

claim: The critical concentration of MinE localization is higher in the planar membrane than in the closed membrane.
source: The linear stability analysis (light shaded area in Figure 5) showed that the critical concentration of MinE localization is higher in the planar membrane.
evidence: This is demonstrated by theoretical analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Under confinement, the shift is sufficiently strong to eliminate wave generation at stronger MinE localization.
source: These results suggested that the condition is dependent on the size of the membrane; under confinement, the shift is sufficiently strong to eliminate wave generation at stronger MinE localization.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the simulation and theoretical analysis results.

claim: Wave generation of the planar membrane was less suppressed, and thus, it continued when there was stronger MinE localization on the membrane.
source: On the other hand, wave generation of the planar membrane was less suppressed, and thus, it continued when there was stronger MinE localization on the membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the simulation and theoretical analysis results.

claim: In the closed geometry, Model I and Model II reproduce the same results, suggesting that under confinement the difference between the models is not important.
source: We found that in the closed geometry, these two models reproduce the same results, suggesting that under confinement the difference between the models is not important.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the two computational models.

claim: Wave generation occurs rather than uniform oscillation in the closed membrane.
source: The phase boundary of the homogeneous oscillation requires higher concentrations than that of the Min wave, resulting in wave generation rather than uniform oscillation in the closed membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the linear stability analysis.

claim: For a small system, the effect of the dynamics of bulk remains only for the zero mode of the spherical membrane.
source: Thus, for a small system, the effect of the dynamics of bulk remains only for the zero mode of the spherical membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the theoretical analysis shown in Figure 7.

claim: The robustness of wave generation in planar membranes against MinE localization is stronger than that predicted by the linear stability analysis.
source: Our numerical simulations suggested that the robustness against MinE localization is stronger than that predicted by the linear stability analysis (Figure 5).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing numerical simulations to linear stability analysis in Figure 5.

claim: One possible reason for the robustness is that the wave generation is dependent on initial perturbation of the concentration fields due to the excitability of the system.
source: One possible reason is that the wave generation is dependent on initial perturbation of the concentration fields due to the excitability of the system.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the simulation results.

claim: The homogeneous stationary state is linearly stable but responds largely against finite perturbation in excitable systems.
source: The homogeneous stationary state is linearly stable but responds largely against finite perturbation (Figure 8).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulations shown in Figure 8.

claim: The instability of the planar membrane starts from a core of wave emergence rather than from uniform oscillation on the planar membrane.
source: In fact, the instability of the planar membrane starts from a core of wave emergence rather than from uniform oscillation on the planar membrane, as observed in a previous study (Loose et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an observation consistent with previous experimental studies, supported by citation.

claim: The closed membrane did not show excitability.
source: In contrast with the planar membrane, the closed membrane did not show excitability (Figure 8B), and this system quickly relaxed to its stationary state without traveling in a large path.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulations shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Excitable systems may exhibit dissipative solitary pulses propagating in one direction with fixed speed, and spiral and turbulent waves in two dimensions.
source: It is known that excitable systems may exhibit dissipative solitary pulses propagating in one direction with fixed speed, and spiral and turbulent waves in two dimensions (Keener, 1980; Bär and Eiswirth, 1993).
evidence: This is established knowledge about excitable systems, supported by citations.

claim: Model II demonstrated a propagating solitary wave when the initial condition was chosen appropriately in one- and two-dimensional membranes.
source: In fact, Model II demonstrated a propagating solitary wave when the initial condition was chosen appropriately in one- (Figure 8C) and two-dimensional (Figure 8D) membranes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulations shown in Figure 8C and D.

claim: A spiral wave was obtained by cutting a solitary band in the two-dimensional membrane.
source: A spiral wave was obtained by cutting a solitary band in the two-dimensional membrane (Figure 8D), a phenomenon which has also been observed in other excitable systems (Winfree, 1991).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulations shown in Figure 8D and is consistent with observations in other excitable systems.

claim: Pulsing between the cytosolic parts and the membrane surface is the initial stage of Min wave emergence in small microdroplets.
source: For small microdroplets that only show a single wave inside, time-lapse imaging of Min proteins showed that pulsing between the cytosolic parts and the membrane surface is the initial stage of Min wave emergence, similar to observations reported previously (Zieske et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an experimental observation consistent with previous reports, supported by citation.

claim: The pulsing pattern transforms to pole-to-pole oscillation, and then, settles into traveling waves.
source: However, our imaging demonstrated that the pulsing pattern transforms to pole-to-pole oscillation, and then, settles into traveling waves.
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 9 and Video 9.

claim: This transition of wave patterns can be recapitulated by computational simulation.
source: This transition of wave patterns is not specific to wet experiments but can be recapitulated by our computational simulation (Figure 9, Video 8).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulations shown in Figure 9 and Video 8.

claim: The introduction or reduction of stochastic noises to the simulation did not change the results.
source: The introduction or reduction of stochastic noises to the simulation did not change the results, indicating that this transition proceeds in a deterministic manner; namely, wave instability underlying reaction-diffusion coupling is the only driving force that leads to the emergence of Min waves in the cell-sized space.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from simulation experiments.

claim: Wave instability underlying reaction-diffusion coupling is the only driving force that leads to the emergence of Min waves in the cell-sized space.
source: The introduction or reduction of stochastic noises to the simulation did not change the results, indicating that this transition proceeds in a deterministic manner; namely, wave instability underlying reaction-diffusion coupling is the only driving force that leads to the emergence of Min waves in the cell-sized space.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from simulation experiments.

claim: The conditions for Min wave appearance are limited in closed cell-sized space as compared with those on a 2D planar membrane.
source: In this study, we show that the conditions for Min wave appearance are limited in closed cell-sized space as compared with those on a 2D planar membrane.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, supported by experimental and theoretical data.

claim: The rate of spontaneous localization of MinE is an important factor in determining the generation of Min waves in cell-sized closed spaces.
source: From experiments and simulation, we have shown that the rate of spontaneous localization of MinE is an important factor in determining the generation of Min waves in cell-sized closed spaces.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, supported by experimental and theoretical data.

claim: Owing to the large surface-area-to-volume in the cell-sized space, localization to the membrane (even for weak interactions) becomes more prominent than it is in the planar membrane system.
source: Owing to the large surface-area-to-volume in the cell-sized space, localization to the membrane (even for weak interactions) becomes more prominent than it is in the planar membrane system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations about size-dependent localization.

claim: Spontaneous localization of MinE on membranes works in an inhibitory manner with respect to the generation of Min waves.
source: Spontaneous localization of MinE on membranes works in an inhibitory manner with respect to the generation of Min waves, but it is suppressed in the presence of a protein crowder, such as BSA or cell extract, resulting in the generation of Min waves.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations about MinE localization and wave generation.

claim: The effect of BSA and cell extract is observed at a relatively low concentration relative to the effect of crowding in the cytoplasm of living cells.
source: This effect is observed at a relatively low concentration (cell extract; 1 mg/mL, BSA; 10 mg/mL) relative to the effect of crowding in the cytoplasm of living cells (100–300 mg/mL equivalent) and is not observed with synthetic polymers such as PEG8000 and Ficoll70.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data comparing different crowding agents.

claim: BSA and cell extract are considered to modify the interaction between MinE and membranes, and the mechanism is different from a major effect of crowding, increase of viscosity.
source: Hence, BSA and cell extract are considered to modify the interaction between MinE and membranes, and the mechanism is different from a major effect of crowding, increase of viscosity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations about different crowding agents.

claim: BSA at high concentration (>10 mg/mL) attaches to the lipid membrane.
source: Because a previous report has indicated that BSA at high concentration (>10 mg/mL) attaches to the lipid membrane (Ruggeri et al., 2013), and as several proteins in cell extract are assumed to interact with such membranes, a plausible explanation of the effect of the protein crowders is competitive inhibition.
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: A plausible explanation of the effect of the protein crowders is competitive inhibition.
source: Because a previous report has indicated that BSA at high concentration (>10 mg/mL) attaches to the lipid membrane (Ruggeri et al., 2013), and as several proteins in cell extract are assumed to interact with such membranes, a plausible explanation of the effect of the protein crowders is competitive inhibition.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the experimental observations.

claim: Tuning lipids conditions to reduce spontaneous MinE attachment on membranes seems to be important for the generation of Min waves without aid from auxiliary molecules.
source: To match this assumption, tuning lipids conditions to reduce spontaneous MinE attachment on membranes (Figure 3F) seems to be important for the generation of Min waves without aid from auxiliary molecules, as reported previously (Zieske et al., 2016; Litschel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations and is consistent with previous reports.

claim: The conformation of MinE is in equilibrium between a free state of membrane targeting sequences (MTS) at the N-terminal (open conformation) and a packed structure (closed conformation).
